items.problem: Calls that go to voicemail and never get called back.
items.fix: A missed call gets a text back in seconds and lands on a list someone works.

items.problem: Quotes that go out and nobody follows up.
items.fix: Every quote gets its follow-up on a schedule, without anyone having to remember.

items.problem: The same job typed into three places.
items.fix: Enter it once. The calendar, the invoice and the books all read from the same record.

items.problem: Paying every month for software that almost fits.
items.fix: A system you own, built around the way you already work, in place of the subscriptions.

items.problem: Customers who can't find you, or find the wrong hours.
items.fix: A fast site and a Google profile that agree with each other and stay current.

items.problem: Departments that each keep their own version of the truth.
items.fix: One platform the office, the field and the books all work from, so a handoff can't drop anything.

systems.heading: Every department. One system.
systems.lede: I build the platform a whole company runs on: estimating, the field, finance, safety, people and equipment working from one record, instead of five tools that don't talk to each other.

caps.title: Connect what you already run
caps.body: Accounting and ERP, Outlook and Microsoft 365, payments, phones and texts. Data goes in once and lands everywhere it's needed.

caps.title: Replace what doesn't fit
caps.body: Screens built around how your departments actually hand work to each other, in place of subscriptions that almost fit.

caps.title: Automate the procedures
caps.body: Approvals, follow-ups, reminders and reports that people currently do from memory.

caps.title: Office and field, one record
caps.body: Phone apps that capture photos, hours and sign-offs where the work happens, and show up in the office the same minute.

caps.title: See the business live
caps.body: What's owed, what's late, and who has the ball, without waiting for someone to build a spreadsheet.

steps.title: Look
steps.body: Twenty minutes, free, at your place or on the phone. You walk me through one job, from the first call to getting paid.

steps.title: Plan
steps.body: In writing: what to fix first, what to ignore, and a fixed price. It's yours to keep, even if you do it yourself.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Nothing goes live until you've seen it. Your current tools keep running until you're ready to switch.

steps.title: Keep it running
steps.body: Hosting, backups, fixes and small changes, monthly. You own all of it: the data, the accounts, the code.

about.heading: Who you'd be working with.
about.body:
I spent ten years running operations before I wrote software. A service lane at a Honda dealership. General manager of a car wash, then a group of them, then a district. Schedules, payroll, and equipment that breaks on the coldest day of the year.

Now I co-found and build software for running construction companies, end to end. This is the same work, for businesses of any size closer to home.

items.name: Knock Em' Down Detailing
items.body: One system built to replace Housecall Pro and QuickBooks: booking, quotes, invoicing, the books, follow-ups, and an iPhone app for the driveway. A new site and brand on top.
